physical_harm: Rape resulting in secondary sexual characteristics development and hymen rupture, but no external injuries
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence adduced by the victim was natural and trustworthy - Positive evidence adduced by the prosecution that A-3 aided the commission of offence by asking the victim to go to her house to take 'lassi' where A-1 and A-2 bolted the room and subjected the victim to rape.
witness_credibility: PW5 (victim) and PW6 (mother of the victim) have been subjected to lengthy cross-examination but nothing has come out to create reasonable doubt in their testimony.
bail_history: Accused/appellants Om Prakash, Kartar Singh and Chhoti were granted bail by this Court vide orders dated 18.5.2009, 20.7.2009 and 16.4.2010 respectively.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: not stated; Trial judgment: 16.12.1996; High Court decision: 30.7.2008; Supreme Court decision: 14.10.2014
legal_representation: Rishi Malhotra, Prem Malhotra for the Appellant; Nupur Chaudhary, Vivekta Singh, Kamal Mohan Gupta for the Respondent
investigation_status: Charge-sheet filed; investigation taken up; first information report registered on 13.6.1995; trial commenced
appeal_history: Trial court: conviction and sentence affirmed; High Court: conviction and sentence affirmed; Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the victim, a 15-year-old girl, was raped by the accused after being lured to the house of accused Chhoti by her. The prosecution presented evidence, including the victim's testimony, medical reports, and witness statements, to establish the commission of the crime and the role of each accused.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the accused were falsely implicated due to enmity, particularly for accused Chhoti, who claimed she was not present during the rape and that the victim's allegations were fabricated. They also challenged the conviction of Chhoti under Section 109 IPC, arguing that mere failure to prevent the crime does not constitute abetment.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the legal principles under Sections 107 and 109 of the Indian Penal Code, which define abetment and the punishment for abetting an offence. The court emphasized that abetment requires intentional aiding or instigation, not mere failure to prevent.
precedent_relied_upon: Ku/want Singh @ Kulbansh Singh vs. State of Bihar (2007) 15 SCC 670: 2007 (7) SCR 1178 and Priya Patel vs. State of M.P. and another (2006) 6 SCC 263: 2006 (3) Suppl. SCR 456
sentencing_rationale: The sentence was imposed based on the conviction under Sections 376(2)(g) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code, with the trial court finding the prosecution's evidence sufficient to establish guilt. The court upheld the sentences as just and appropriate given the circumstances.
